changelog: Add a principle that strongly deprioritizes any boundary where the left fragment alone would contradict or reverse the whole sentence — to address the primary finding that contradiction was underweighted.
Add a principle banning cuts that split lexical words, bound morphemes, or separate a content word from its immediately attached particles/auxiliaries — to stop fragmentary, incoherent pieces.

Add a conditional guideline allowing denser cuts in very short‑latency contexts only when the right fragment is independently interpretable (a short, self‑contained continuation) — to recover short‑bin density without encouraging unsafe predicate splits.

C3: added an explicit ban on cutting inside lexical words, bound morphemes, or between a content word and its immediately attached particles/auxiliaries to stop fragmentary, incoherent pieces (addresses the primary finding).

C8: made contradiction a decisive de‑prioritizer (treat boundaries where the left fragment alone would contradict/negate/reverse the sentence as effectively invalid) and added a conditional dense‑cut allowance for very short‑latency settings only when the right fragment is independently interpretable (addresses underweighted contra and short‑latency loss).

Replace E1 with labeled example ja_jp_96 to teach the scorer about dangerous cuts that fragment lexical words/particles in short‑latency (≤5) contexts — addresses the finding that the prompt failed to forbid internal-word/particle fragmentation.

Replace E2 with labeled example ja_jp_955 to expose a ≤3 short‑latency case where contradiction risk is decisive, so scorers learn to avoid boundaries whose left fragment alone would reverse/negate the sentence — addresses the underweighted contradiction finding and the primary short‑latency issue.

Replace E3 with labeled example ja_jp_346 to show a case where early cuts can misassign roles or leave predicate structure incomplete, reinforcing that safe dense cuts must still preserve independent interpretability of the right fragment.

Replace E4 with labeled example ja_jp_561 to add another ≤5 measured case emphasizing both particle/auxiliary attachment and contradiction risk so scorers prefer dense but safe boundaries rather than fragmentary or high‑contra ones.

Append a principle that makes contradiction a near‑veto for high ranks: if the left fragment taken alone contradicts/negates/reverses the whole sentence, treat that boundary as unacceptable for top placements — addresses the primary finding that contra was underweighted.

Append a principle banning internal‑word/particle fragmentation: do not cut inside lexical words, bound morphemes, or between a content word and its immediately attached particles/auxiliaries — addresses the failure to forbid internal fragmentation.

Append a conditional dense‑cut guideline that says what a good dense cut looks like (right fragment must be independently interpretable and not begin with predicate‑final auxiliaries/negation), so short‑latency density can be recovered safely without blanket bans — addresses short‑latency loss while avoiding an absolute penalty on predicate/argument splits.
Replace Example E1 with measured labeled example ja_jp_933 so scorers see a real case where contradiction and attachment mistakes matter directly.
